961: C is correct because AWS WAF integrates directly with an Application Load Balancer, and a rate-based rule automatically counts requests from each source IP address and blocks them once the rate exceeds a defined threshold, which is the standard managed way to mitigate volumetric DDoS traffic. AWS WAF cannot be attached directly to a Global Accelerator accelerator, so the ALB is the valid and simplest integration point. Configuring a web ACL with rate-based rules requires far less implementation effort than building custom Lambda logic with network ACLs or rearchitecting the traffic flow with CloudFront.
962: B is correct because the AWS Glue DynamoDB export connector leverages the DynamoDB table export feature, which reads data out to Amazon S3 without consuming the table's provisioned read or write capacity, so daily metric calculations have minimal effect on the table's throughput. A Glue job running on a recurring schedule can compute the performance metrics from the exported data, whereas the other options would scan the table directly and consume provisioned capacity or require heavy infrastructure.
963: C is correct because an Amazon SQS queue durably stores the job items and decouples the producers from the processing instances, satisfying both the loose coupling and durable storage requirements. An Auto Scaling policy based on the number of items in the SQS queue, such as a target tracking policy on the ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible metric, adds EC2 instances when jobs back up and removes them when the queue drains, so processing runs in parallel at the right scale, whereas SNS topics do not durably hold jobs for workers to pull.
964: D is correct because Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate deploys the containerized application in a modular, scalable microservices-style architecture without managing any underlying servers, giving the least operational overhead. Amazon RDS with a Multi-AZ deployment keeps the structured database schemas in a highly available managed relational database, and Amazon S3 provides scalable, durable object storage for the product data and product images.
965: A is correct because client-side encryption with customer managed keys encrypts the data in the client application before it is ever transmitted to Amazon S3, which is exactly what is required when data must be encrypted before being stored. Using customer managed keys also gives the company full control over key policies, rotation, and auditability through AWS KMS, whereas the server-side options only encrypt the data after it reaches S3.
966: B is correct because EMR runtime roles, available with EMR on EC2 clusters, assign each team's big data workload an application-scoped IAM role with only the specific permissions that team needs. Runtime role credentials are delivered through the EMR runtime rather than through the EC2 instance metadata service, so the workloads cannot access IMDSv2 on the underlying instances and each team is isolated to its required AWS services.
967: A is correct because an Amazon SQS FIFO queue between the web tier and the worker tier durably buffers the submitted forms, so no data is lost even if workers fail or are restarted. FIFO queues provide exactly-once processing through content-based deduplication and idempotency handling, and they preserve message order, which together guarantee that each form is processed quickly and exactly once.
968: D is correct because Amazon Kinesis Data Streams is the AWS native service for durably ingesting and processing streaming data in real time from many producers. Amazon OpenSearch Service is purpose built for real-time full-text search and analytics on the ingested data, and Amazon QuickSight provides managed visualizations, so the pipeline keeps the search and visualization features updated in near real time.
969: A is correct because AWS App2Container is purpose built to containerize existing ASP.NET applications with minimal effort by automatically generating the container image and deployment resources. Deploying the containerized application with a CloudFormation template to Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate removes the need to provision or manage any servers, allows scaling based on CloudWatch metrics, and minimizes operational maintenance of the modernized .NET application.
970: D is correct because AWS Secrets Manager is the AWS managed service purpose built for storing, retrieving, and rotating credentials such as employee usernames and passwords, and the BatchGetSecretValue API efficiently retrieves multiple secrets in a single call. Using CloudFormation with Secrets Manager keeps credential storage and retrieval fully managed with the least operational overhead, whereas Parameter Store is intended for configuration data rather than secrets.
971: D is correct because an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket as origin caches the software files at edge locations close to each remote Outposts server, so downloads are served from the nearest edge location instead of the origin bucket in ap-northeast-1, which significantly reduces deployment latency for servers worldwide. This fully managed configuration requires the least operational overhead, and signed URLs keep the downloads controlled.
972: C is correct because an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP Multi-AZ file system provides highly available, low-latency block storage over the iSCSI protocol that EC2 instances in both Availability Zones can access. It gives the active and standby instances shared block storage with built-in synchronous replication across Availability Zones, requiring far less implementation effort than manually configuring Windows clustering with application-level or EBS-level replication, since EBS volumes are confined to a single Availability Zone.
973: A is correct because the security group on the internet-facing ALB must allow inbound HTTPS traffic on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0 so that users on the public internet can reach the ALB. C is correct because the ALB must allow outbound HTTPS traffic on port 443 to the web application instances' security group so it can forward traffic to the application servers. E is correct because the ALB health checks run over HTTPS on port 8443, which requires an outbound rule to the instances on that port, and inbound rules from the instances are unnecessary because the ALB initiates both the forwarded traffic and the health checks.
974: A is correct because CloudFront requires TLS certificates for custom domain names to be provisioned with AWS Certificate Manager in the us-east-1 Region, regardless of where the S3 origin bucket resides. D is correct because origin access control (OAC) is the recommended way to restrict the S3 bucket so uploads and other requests can only be made through the CloudFront distribution, allowing the photo uploads over the custom domain while keeping the bucket private.
975: A is correct because Amazon Athena is a serverless query service that runs standard SQL directly against the Parquet files in Amazon S3 and can be configured to read and decrypt files protected with client-side encryption using KMS managed keys. With no infrastructure to manage and pay-per-query pricing based only on the data scanned, Athena is the most cost-effective choice for occasional queries such as computing moving averages for a specific calendar day, whereas Redshift Spectrum and EMR Serverless add unnecessary cost and S3 Select is not suited to this analysis.
976: B is correct because an Amazon Route 53 geoproximity routing policy routes DNS traffic based on the geographic location of the user and the AWS resources, directing each user to the Region where the closest EC2 instances are running. Within each Region, the internet-facing Network Load Balancer then distributes the traffic across all Availability Zones, so users around the world are consistently sent to the deployment nearest their location.
977: A is correct because Amazon RDS for MySQL supports encryption at rest using AWS KMS managed keys through a simple managed setting, and SSL/TLS certificates encrypt the database connections in transit. Provisioning and managing the SSL/TLS certificates with AWS Certificate Manager keeps both layers of encryption fully handled by AWS services, which meets the security mandate with the least operational overhead compared to IPsec tunnels, VPNs, or third-party application-level encryption.
978: D is correct because AWS Backup is a fully managed service that can create a backup plan for Amazon RDS with a 90-day retention period to meet the regulatory data retention requirement, while its continuous backups support point-in-time restore to satisfy the 14-day restore requirement. This gives centralized, automated compliance with the least operational overhead, whereas RDS automated backups have a maximum retention of 35 days, and manual snapshots and Aurora clones do not provide point-in-time restore.
979: B is correct because Amazon Aurora Serverless automatically and instantly scales database capacity up and down based on actual usage, which matches a variable, read-heavy workload with occasional writes and steady growth. Aurora Serverless is a managed relational database that only charges for the capacity actually consumed, making it more cost-effective than always-on provisioned RDS storage classes, and it preserves the relational model the application requires, unlike DynamoDB.
980: C is correct because a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 attached to the VPC provides a private, highly available path from the EC2 instances to S3 without traversing the internet or requiring NAT infrastructure. Updating the IAM instance profile policy with a Deny action on the s3:ResourceAccount condition key blocks access to any bucket that is not owned by the company's AWS account, ensuring the application can only access the company's own buckets with the least operational overhead.
